newsitem.title: UK: Princess Diana flies secretly to sunshine hideaway.
newsitem.headline: Princess Diana flies secretly to sunshine hideaway.

text.p: Princess Diana slipped out of Britain secretly earlier this week with an aide to spend Christmas soaking up the sunshine on her favourite Caribbean holiday island of Barbuda, newspapers reported on Friday.

Diana, divorced this year from heir-to-the-throne Prince Charles, turned down an invitation from Queen Elizabeth to join the rest of the royal family for their traditional Christmas gathering at Sandringham estate in eastern England.
But she phoned her sons, Prince William, 14, and Prince Harry, 12, to see how they liked their presents, said the Daily Mirror.
The tabloid quoted an unidentified friend of Diana as saying: "There was nothing discourteous in refusing the Queen's invitation. Diana felt her presence would put a strain on things.
"As her sons were with Charles, there was nothing to keep her in Britain."
Newspapers said the 35-year-old princess, who spent last Christmas Day alone at London's Kensington Palace, jetted off to the Caribbean with her personal assistant Victoria Mendham, 27.
The Daily Mail said the pair slipped undetected out of frosty Britain on Christmas Eve for the sunny Caribbean as speculation swirled through the media that Diana was planning a holiday in Australia.
"She had made no attempt to contravene the false rumour and had even encouraged it by booking seats on a flight to Australia," said the paper.
It said she boarded a flight to Antigua, en route to Barbuda, "without anyone noting her presence, choosing to travel economy rather than first class".
Newspapers said Diana was sharing a 1,700 pound ($2,844) a night beachside villa at the exclusive K Club on Barbuda with Mendham.
"Her privacy is almost guaranteed and the staff go out of their way to protect her," the Daily Mail quoted a friend of the princess as saying. ($1=.5977 Pound)
